title: Fleet allocation playbook and utilization narratives for throughput contracts
creator: Dmitri Korovin
description: Problem: Customers buying Dedicated capacity often request throughput SLAs (tokens/s or requests/s) but the fleet-level commitment and autoscale rules we currently expose are coarse. We see over-provisioning (wasted cost) or tight provisioning (latency SLO breaches) depending on tenant burstiness. Goal: Produce a prescriptive playbook and automation artifacts that map tenant throughput contracts to fleet allocation recipes, autoscale policy profiles, and a compact utilization "narrative" that operators and customers can read and act on. Deliverables: 1) Fleet Allocation Playbook (documented step-by-step rules for converting throughput guarantees and p95 latency SLOs into slot/gpu counts by pool, including headroom and pre-warm buffers). 2) Autoscale Policy Profiles (a small set of tested policy templates: conservative, balanced, and aggressive) with parameter knobs and expected cost/latency trade-offs. 3) Utilization Narratives (auto-generated natural language summaries and one-line actions per pool for Console: e.g., "Pool A: 65% sustained utilization, safe to downscale by 1 slot during 02:00-08:00 PST; enable burst floor of 10% for 3 hours"). 4) Simulation harness and sample runs (CSV + dashboard) that show cost delta across templates for representative tenant traces. 5) Recommendation engine prototype that surfaces a ranked list of adjustments (reduce commit, switch template, schedule burst windows). Constraints: must work with existing Dedicated control plane APIs (no infra changes), use existing telemetry (token counts, p95 latencies, per-tenant slot usage), and fit into a 2-phase rollout (read-only suggestions -> automated apply behind feature flag).
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with worked examples converting throughput guarantees to slot counts
Three autoscale policy templates implemented as JSON policy artifacts and validated in staging
Utilization narrative generator integrated with Console backend endpoint and visible in staging dashboard
Simulation harness reproduces at least 8 representative tenant traces and emits cost/latency delta CSVs
Recommendation UI surfaces top-3 actions per pool and a 'preview cost impact' metric
Runbook for safe rollback and operator checks documented and reviewed by SRE
notes: Trade-offs: conservative template minimizes incidents but increases cost; aggressive template reduces cost but accepts higher p95 tail risk. We'll provide expected failure modes for each.
Decision: start with a deterministic formula (capacity = baseline qps * safety_factor + prewarm) and layer ML/heuristics only after stable telemetry is available.
Data needs: per-tenant time-series of requests/s, tokens/s, p95 latency, and slot occupancy. We may need 30 days of retention for reliable percentile estimation.
Edge cases: bursty tenants that cross regions; we will propose a cross-region burst floor and require customer opt-in for cross-region autoscale
Cost model: use current slot-hour price + estimated token execution cost; simulation will include both to illustrate total ops impact
